meta.description: Loads mass-spectrometry data into Python/R and strips search-engine bookkeeping before values are trusted; supports MaxQuant proteinGroups, DIA-NN reports, and mzML/mzXML while enforcing quantification and missingness contracts.
meta.audit_type: independent scientific re-audit of immutable source
meta.execution_note: All seven input cases were executed. The exact bundled QFeatures example exited 0 in WSL; the auxiliary native Windows reproduction printed correct output and then failed during teardown with exit 139 as the Skill warns.

scientific_integrity.detail: No output fabricated identifiers, performance figures, sample sizes, or statistical results; every reported value came from a retained execution log.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill and all outputs remained within technical proteomics import and missingness diagnosis, with no individual diagnosis, prescription, or clinical triage.

methodological_ground.detail: The executed routes enforced MaxQuant bookkeeping removal, zero-to-missing conversion, DIA-NN run and global protein-group FDR, corrected TMT reporter selection, and abundance-dependent missingness diagnosis.

code_usability.detail: All Python workflows and the exact bundled QFeatures example ran in supported environments. The known native Windows teardown crash is explicitly classified as failure and has a verified WSL route with exit 0.

functional_suitability.note: The advertised MaxQuant, DIA-NN, mzML/mzXML, TMT, and R routes are present and correct; the QFeatures route does not remove 55 all-missing protein groups as the Python LFQ route does.

reliability.note: Format, column-family, precursor, global-FDR, zero, and wrong-table failures are handled explicitly with repeatable outcomes.

performance_context.note: The workflow is linear and efficient, although the 317-line SKILL.md duplicates some runnable-example detail inline.

agent_usability.note: Scenario routing and failure prevention are strong; feedback and row-accounting are slightly inconsistent between Python and QFeatures.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger phrases, a usage guide, explicit prerequisites, and actionable failures make the Skill discoverable and recoverable.

security.note: All demonstrated operations are local and read-only on input data, with no credentials, code-string execution, or destructive operations.

maintainability.note: Four packaged examples provide deterministic verification; inline and packaged copies of the same workflows create a small drift risk.

agent_specific.note: Triggering, scope boundaries, related-skill routing, idempotency, and stop conditions are precise; progressive disclosure could move more detail out of SKILL.md.

key_strengths: Every original regression case now completes with the intended FDR, zero, precursor, and missingness contracts.
The exact packaged QFeatures route has a clean, repeatable WSL execution with explicit R, QFeatures, and cli versions.
Fresh TMT and wrong-table cases demonstrate correct scope routing and defensive validation.
The Skill explicitly treats the reproducible native Windows teardown crash as failure and gives a verified supported alternative.

recommendations.title: Align QFeatures valid-row filtering with Python
recommendations.problem: After zeroIsNA and logTransform, the bundled QFeatures example retains 55 protein groups with no quantified value, returning 1500 rows where the Python route returns 1445.
recommendations.root_cause: The R workflow stops after transformation and does not apply the documented valid-value rule used by the Python LFQ workflow.
recommendations.fix: After creating log2LFQ, subset that assay to rows with at least one non-missing sample and report pre-bookkeeping, post-bookkeeping, and quantified row counts. Add an assertion that no delivered row is all missing.
